USGS Water Data API responses (US Government work, public domain), recorded
with curl and Python's urllib from https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov without a
key (api-version 1.10.3). Every file is the response body byte for byte,
except the two marked "cut" below. Times in the requests are UTC.

C = /ogcapi/v1/collections/continuous/items?
D = /ogcapi/v1/collections/daily/items?
M = /ogcapi/v1/collections/combined-metadata/items?
V = &properties=time,value,approval_status,qualifier&skipGeometry=true
S = &properties=id,parameter_code,parameter_name,statistic_id,primary,
    unit_of_measure,begin,end&skipGeometry=true&limit=50000&f=json
Q = 66a4e3fb8abe42fcb0942b5c0fe98f68 (USGS-01646500, 00060, instantaneous)
R = 2cf409b0d9694c01828f5d4ff14586a5 (USGS-01646500, 00060, daily mean)

Copied from docs/provider-apis/ (recorded 2026-10-06):
  continuous_full_properties.json  usgs_continuous_items.json (every
                                   property, geometry, limit=4)
  continuous_slim_page1.json       usgs_continuous_slim_page1.json (a cursor
                                   next link)
  daily_full_properties.json       usgs_daily_items.json
  error_property_not_found.json    usgs_error_unknown_property.json (the
                                   older wording of the 400)

Recorded 2026-10-15, 23:02-23:12Z:

Paging. With `sortby` the API serves only the first page: its next link is
`offset=` and following it is a 400. Without `sortby`, continuous pages
follow `cursor=` links in time order, and a full last page carries an
`offset=<limit>` link without a cursor; following it reads from that offset
of the window's start again.
  continuous_chain_page1.json      C time_series_id=Q&datetime=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z
                                   /2026-10-01T00:29:59Z V&limit=2&f=json
  continuous_chain_page2.json      its next link (a cursor)
  continuous_chain_page3.json      its next link (a cursor); full, with an
                                   offset=2 link
  continuous_chain_page4_echo.json that offset link: 00:10 and 00:15 again,
                                   with page 2's cursor link (a cycle)
  continuous_full_last_page.json   C time_series_id=Q&datetime=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z
                                   /2026-10-01T00:14:59Z V&limit=3&f=json:
                                   three values, full, an offset=3 link
  continuous_after_offset_link.json
                                   that offset link: an empty page, no link
  continuous_sortby_page1.json     as continuous_chain_page1 with
                                   &sortby=time: an offset link
  error_sortby_second_page.json    that link: HTTP 400, "Only the first page
                                   of data can be returned when specifying
                                   'sortby'"
  daily_chain_page1.json           D time_series_id=R&datetime=2026-09-20
                                   /2026-09-30 V&limit=4&f=json: days in
                                   feature-id order (26, 27, 22, 28)
  daily_chain_page2.json           its next link (29, 25, 20, 21)
  daily_chain_page3.json           its next link (23, 30, 24), no link
The datetime interval is closed: ...T00:00:00Z/...T00:10:00Z gave 00:00,
00:05 and 00:10; .../...T00:09:59Z gave two values.

Values:
  continuous_dst.json              C time_series_id=Q&datetime=2025-11-02T05:30:00Z
                                   /2025-11-02T06:29:59Z V&limit=50000&f=json
                                   (EDT ended at 06:00Z: the 5-minute grid
                                   holds)
  daily_dst.json                   D time_series_id=R&datetime=2025-11-01
                                   /2025-11-03 V&limit=50000&f=json
  continuous_estimated.json        C monitoring_location_id=USGS-05331000
                                   &parameter_code=00060&datetime=
                                   2023-01-01T00:00:00Z/2023-01-01T02:00:00Z
                                   V&f=json (no limit: the API sends 10;
                                   `qualifier` is an array, ["ESTIMATED"])
  daily_estimated.json             D monitoring_location_id=USGS-05331000
                                   &parameter_code=00060&statistic_id=00003
                                   &datetime=2023-01-01/2023-01-10
                                   &properties=time,value,approval_status,
                                   qualifier,time_series_id&skipGeometry=true
                                   &f=json (ten values, full: offset link)
  continuous_empty.json            C monitoring_location_id=USGS-15514000
                                   &parameter_code=00060&datetime=
                                   2024-01-15T00:00:00Z/2024-01-15T01:00:00Z
                                   V&f=json (no values: numberReturned 0)

Series (combined-metadata). `begin` and `end` are instants (the site's
midnight in UTC for daily series); `primary` is "Primary" or null; USGS marks
every epoch of a series Primary (USGS-01646500 has three Primary
instantaneous water-temperature series), and USGS-12175000 two Primary gage
heights (web_description "Primary" and "Secondary").
  series_by_id.json                M monitoring_location_id=USGS-01646500&id=Q S
  series_by_parameter.json         M monitoring_location_id=USGS-01646500
                                   &parameter_code=00060&statistic_id=00011 S
  series_none.json                 M monitoring_location_id=USGS-02431011&id=Q S
                                   (another site's id: no row)
  series_site.json                 M monitoring_location_id=USGS-01646500
                                   &data_type=Continuous values,Daily values S
                                   (68 rows)
  series_site_unfiltered.json      M monitoring_location_id=USGS-01646500
                                   &properties=id,parameter_code,parameter_name,
                                   statistic_id,computation_identifier,primary,
                                   unit_of_measure,begin,end&skipGeometry=true
                                   &limit=50000&f=json (73 rows: also three
                                   field-measurement rows with UUID ids and
                                   two peak rows without a statistic)
  series_several_primary.json      M monitoring_location_id=USGS-12175000
                                   &parameter_code=00065&statistic_id=00011 S

Catalog (combined-metadata with geometry). The whole catalog query,
M parameter_code=00060,00065,62620,62619&statistic_id=00011&properties=
monitoring_location_id,monitoring_location_name,id,parameter_code,
parameter_name,statistic_id,primary,unit_of_measure,begin,end&limit=50000
&f=json, returned 29,017 rows of 17,438 sites on one page (20.2 MB, 2.8 s;
00060 14,632, 00065 14,168, 62620 184, 62619 33; 707 rows not Primary;
1,132 without begin and end; 16 without geometry; 343 sites with several
Primary series of one parameter). It is not committed.
  catalog_bbox.json                that query with &bbox=-76.4,36.8,-76.2,37.0
                                   (14 rows, 10 sites)
  catalog_page1.json .. catalog_page3.json
                                   the same with limit=5 (cursor links)
  catalog_null_geometry.json       cut: the 16 rows of the whole catalog
                                   whose geometry is null, in the envelope of
                                   that response (re-serialized by Python's
                                   json, two-space indent; next link removed)

Refusals (HTTP status, body):
  error_invalid_key.json           403, header X-Api-Key: notakey0123456789:
                                   api.data.gov's {"error":{"code":
                                   "API_KEY_INVALID",...}}
  error_time_envelope.json         400, C ...&datetime=2020-01-01T00:00:00Z
                                   /2023-01-06T00:00:00Z
  error_limit.json                 400, C ...&limit=100000
  error_unknown_property.json      400, C ...&properties=time,nosuch
  error_collection_not_found.json  404, /ogcapi/v1/collections/nosuch/items
  error_datetime.json              400, C ...&datetime=yesterday

Units (unit_of_measure) over the CONUS series of combined-metadata
(bbox=-125,24,-66,50, first 50,000 rows): ft, ft^3/s, degC, uS/cm, mg/l, in,
pH Units, _FNU, %, tons/day, ppt, degF, Acre-ft, RFU, ug/l, ft/s, mph, deg,
mmHg, m, m/s, mbar, hPa, kn, m^3/s, kPa, psi, inHg and others. The
parameter-codes collection spells some differently: ft3/s, deg C, ft/sec,
m3/sec, Deg.

Fuzz seeds (tests/fixtures/io/usgs_items, usgs_catalog, rfc3339 and
tests/fixtures/fetch/usgs_paging) are these files with a first byte that
picks the reader, or pages joined by 0xFF. large_continuous_page.seed is cut:
the first 3,000 values of C time_series_id=000c816dd1d24df2b174f984b57a08d1
(USGS-01485755, 62620) &datetime=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z/2025-12-31T23:59:59Z V
&limit=50000&f=json (a full page: 50,000 values, 14 MB);
large_catalog_page.seed the first 1,300 rows of the whole catalog.
